title: LinkedIn Notes
lede: Public writing from the same desk. Each card is a field note you can open on LinkedIn.

items.title: What “real-time healthcare AI” actually means on a wearable patch
items.excerpt: Streaming ECG and SpO2 is the easy sentence. The hard part is the pipeline: denoise on-device, keep latency honest, and return a risk score a clinician can challenge — not a black box.
items.imageAlt: Cognivus Labs wearable patch used for ECG and SpO2 sensing

items.title: MCP servers are just APIs with manners
items.excerpt: If a model can call tools, the tool schema is the product. Typed inputs, tight auth, and boring errors beat a clever prompt every time. That is the intern work I am doing at Zelora.
items.imageAlt: Interface of an AI tooling product with structured outputs

items.title: IntelliHack 5.0: ten teams left, 350+ started
items.excerpt: OutlierRejects made the finals. The lesson I kept: a model that you can explain to a judge in 90 seconds usually beats a model you can only defend in a notebook.
items.imageAlt: IntelliHack 5.0 team OutlierRejects at the finals

items.title: Vector search is not magic. It is a data contract.
items.excerpt: Finished MongoDB’s AI and Vector Search path. Embeddings only help if the chunking, metadata, and evaluation set are treated as first-class artifacts — same as any other dataset.
items.imageAlt: MongoDB AI and Vector Search certificate awarded to Rivindu Ashinsa

items.title: Pitching Cognivus Labs at Hult Prize
items.excerpt: A clinical monitoring platform has to sound like a product, not a research poster. The qualifier forced the story into one sentence: live waveforms in, decisions a doctor can act on out.
items.imageAlt: Cognivus Labs team pitching at the Hult Prize qualifier
